title: Nature of Matter: Elements, Compounds, and Mixtures

concepts.learning_objective: Define a mixture and its components, and state that components keep their properties and do not react chemically.
Distinguish uniform mixtures from non-uniform mixtures using everyday examples.
Recognise alloys such as stainless steel, brass and bronze as uniform mixtures of metals.
Describe air as a uniform mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
Explain how lime water turning milky shows the presence of carbon dioxide in air.
Explain that dust particles are suspended in air as pollutants and are not an integral part of it.

topics.title: Types of Mixtures and Pure Substances

concepts.learning_objective: Classify mixtures by the physical states of their components and as uniform or non-uniform.
Contrast the everyday meaning of 'pure' with the scientific meaning of a pure substance.
Explain what adulteration is, why it is done and how it harms consumers.
Interpret the electrolysis of water and the tests that identify hydrogen and oxygen.
Describe elements as made of identical atoms that often combine to form molecules.
Recall facts about the number of elements, their states at room temperature and their classification.
Explain that a compound is formed when elements combine in a fixed ratio and has new properties.
Infer from the heating of sugar that it is a compound of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

topics.title: Mixture and Compound of Iron and Sulfur

concepts.learning_objective: Compare a mixture of iron and sulfur with the compound iron sulfide formed on heating.
Identify the gases given off when the mixture and the compound react with dilute hydrochloric acid.

topics.title: Uses of Elements, Compounds and Mixtures; Minerals

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the properties of elements, compounds and mixtures to their uses in daily life and technology.
Describe minerals, including native minerals that are pure elements, and their uses.
